# Deep Crawl intake

First-run setup before any repo scan or ChatGPT Pro dispatch.

## Problem this bot solves
People blow Codex/Astra limits in 1–2 days while ChatGPT GPT 6 Pro allotment is still available. This bot spends that leftover Pro capacity on real research instead of letting it idle.

## Not Research Harness
This product is ChatGPT Pro leftover allotment via the browser (repo scan → RQ queue → Pro session). It is not Research Harness (BYO host / CLI scratch wire-up).

## Collect (one at a time when missing)
1. Repo or local project path the installer wants scanned for research topics.
2. Research queue file (default portable name: `tasks/research-queue.md`) and writeup folder (default: `docs/research/`).
3. Confirm ChatGPT browser account has GPT 6 Pro (or current Pro model) available; human owns login/passkey.
4. Cadence: on-demand vs every-other-day expansion branches.
5. Outbound: draft-only; stage any external send for human go.

## Share / public-export block
Strip personal identity, private repo hostnames, real emails, API keys, and company brand pitches. Sample queue entries use placeholder topics only. Export this public clone only — never a personal Deep Crawl seat with live credentials.

## Rules
- Never scrape ChatGPT passwords or paste cookies into chat.
- Never burn Codex/Astra for the research pass when the point is to use Pro in the browser.
- Do not invent citations in writeups.

# Deep Crawl repo topic scan

Scan the installer's repo for research-worthy topics. Grok does the scan; ChatGPT Pro does the deep research later.

## How to scan
1. Read existing `tasks/research-queue.md` (or installer-named queue) so you do not duplicate open RQ entries.
2. Survey docs, SPECs, TODOs, open questions, and "unknown/deferred" notes.
3. Propose new RQ-### candidates: Topic, Source, Why this matters, Why queued not active, Natural owner, Status.

## Output
Append draft RQ entries to the research queue as DRAFT until the operator confirms. Prefer fewer high-signal topics over a flood.

## Never
- Invent repo facts that are not in the tree.
- Auto-merge speculative topics without operator review on first run.
- Dump secrets, credentials, or private URLs into the queue.

# Deep Crawl ChatGPT Pro dispatch

Run a queued research topic in the ChatGPT browser on GPT 6 Pro (or the installer's current Pro model). This is how leftover Pro allotment gets used after Codex/Astra is exhausted.

## Steps
1. Pick one confirmed RQ topic (or operator-named question).
2. Open ChatGPT in the box browser; confirm Pro model is selected. If login/passkey is needed, stop for human help — never scrape credentials.
3. Paste a tight research brief (question, constraints, ask for sources + UNKNOWN gaps).
4. Save the result as a writeup under `docs/research/` (or installer path) with VERIFIED / INFERRED / UNKNOWN labels where possible.
5. Update the RQ status in the research queue.

## Citations
If Pro gives no source, or a fetch fails, label that claim BLOCKED or UNKNOWN. Never invent citations.

## Spend / allotment
Track that this lane is for ChatGPT Pro browser use, not Codex CLI. If Pro is capped or unavailable: BLOCKED | ChatGPT Pro | ask human. Do not silently fall back to burning Codex.

## Never
- Paste API keys, cookies, or passwords into the ChatGPT thread.
- Claim a citation you did not get from the Pro session or a fetched source.
- Auto-send results outside the operator chat without explicit go.

# Deep Crawl export gate

Before Share-as-template or public export of Deep Crawl.

## Share skill allowlist (ONLY these)
- deep-crawl-intake
- deep-crawl-repo-scan
- deep-crawl-chatgpt-pro-dispatch
- deep-crawl-export-gate

Exclude Research Harness skills, research-alternatives, and any live-seat personal skills.

## Strip
Personal emails / account handles, private hostnames, passkeys, cookies, real RQ topics with customer/PII, company brand ads.

## Keep
Codex-burned / Pro-leftover pitch, portable queue paths (`tasks/research-queue.md`, `docs/research/`), browser Pro dispatch rails, draft-only outbound.

## Auto-send
Off by default. Enabling needs in-thread yes naming destination. Agent messaging and fan-out need per-message go naming who.
